newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, MidEast trading said underway.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, MidEast trading said underway.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Thursday as market talk suggested Middle East trading for May was underway.
Traders heard talk that a western and a Japanese trader sold a cargo each of May Oman crude to China at MPM +2 cents.
The deals were unconfirmed and some traders said they were surprised China had come out to buy so early, which was against its normal practice.
Traders said two majors were also heard to have exchanged a cargo of May Oman at MPM flat.
Other Middle East grades were not talked, traders said.
The near term weakness in Brent and WTI continued to play on the Dubai market where intermonth spreads came in again.
May/June Dubai spread came in to 10/20 cents from a day-earlier 15/23, while June/July came in to 5/13 from 12/15.
The most-active May Brent/Dubai was quoted at $1.40/$1.50, steady from a day before.
Balance March paper Tapis rose 20 cents to be quoted at $21.50/$21.80, although two traders exchange balance March at $21.80.
Regional grades were quiet, with little Minas now believed left available for March.
Players were waiting for Pertamina to allocate exports for April.
Traders said they expected a weak month for April trading, but not as weak as March, as Pertamina looks to sift stocks into the market.
Buyers were actively examining West African imports owing to the weakness of the Brent/Dubai.

A South Korean refinery has taken a VLCC of Odudu/Lokele for loading at the end of the first week of April. The price was on a delivered basis. --Singapore Newsroom (+65 870 3081), Tokyo, M.Yoshikawa (+813 5473 3708)
